title: Arjuna chooses Krishna
hookLine: Duryodhana and Arjuna reach Krishna's bedside on the same errand, and Arjuna picks Krishna over an army
carry: bhakti: want God himself, not just his gifts
tomorrow: how little will Yudhishthira ask for peace?

lines: THE HEAD OF THE BED, THE FOOT.
cards: Two cousins walk into the same bedroom, a few moments apart. Krishna is asleep in his palace at Dwaraka. Duryodhana arrives first and takes a fine seat at the head of the bed.
Arjuna comes in after him and stands at the foot of the bed, hands folded. Both have come for the same thing: Krishna's help in the war that now looks likely. Both wait.
Krishna wakes, and the first person his eyes fall on is Arjuna.

teach.b: Udyoga is a Sanskrit word for effort, for getting ready, and this book of the epic is all preparation: for peace, if it can be found, and for war, if it can't.

It started in Virata's hall, where the families talked it through. Balarama, Krishna's brother, said the Pandavas should ask gently, since Yudhishthira had chosen to play that game. Satyaki answered him hotly.
King Drupada said: send an envoy, and gather allies too. So both sides go looking for friends, and both end up at Krishna's bed. Krishna makes them an offer.

On one side, a huge army of his own fighting men. On the other, Krishna himself, alone, and he will not take up a weapon in the fight. Arjuna may choose first, he says: he saw him first, and he's the younger.
He chooses Krishna, unarmed. Duryodhana is delighted. He gets the army, and leaves thinking he's won the better half.
Now think about what each cousin was really asking for. Duryodhana wanted strength he could count. Arjuna wanted the person.

This is one of the best-loved pictures of bhakti, devotion, in Hindu teaching. Many teachers put it simply: the devotee wants God himself, not only what God can give. Duryodhana walked away with the gifts.
Arjuna walked away with the giver, and Krishna will drive his chariot when the war comes.

teach.h: BHAKTI: THE GIVER, NOT THE GIFTS
teach.b: And look back at the bedroom: one man sat at the head, where rank sits; the other stood at the feet, hands folded. It's why so many Hindus bow at the feet of the Lord.

how: Some Hindu teachers retell Arjuna's choice of Krishna over Krishna's army as a picture of devotion: choosing the Lord himself over what the Lord can give.

games.q: you have one quiet minute at the temple. by Arjuna's choice at the bedside, what does bhakti look like at its heart?
o: list everything you need, quickly, before the minute ends.
fold your hands and want Krishna himself; any asking comes after.
skip it; a prayer without a request doesn't count.
games.why: asking isn't wrong in Hindu prayer. but bhakti at its heart wants the Lord himself, the way Arjuna chose Krishna over an army.

practice: Fold your hands, the way Arjuna stood at the foot of the bed.
Softly say one name of God a few times, Krishna, or the name your family uses, breathing slowly, and this once, ask for nothing: no fix, no favor, just the one you're calling.
If you don't pray, bring to mind someone you love, and notice that you want them, not what they can do for you.
